transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
End: ~16:53 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (CSM), Evan Park (Lead ML Eng, Blue Harbor), Carla Mendes (Infra Manager), Sophie Leung (PM)

Summary:
- Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning: continuous batching, concurrency targets, and queueing behavior under burst
- SE pushed a new batch profile; customer to run 24h steady-state test in staging with modified concurrency
- Identified a tail latency spike correlated with bundle-level KV cache misses and aggressive concurrency at 48 threads

Topics:
- Recap of last week's changes and metrics
- New batch_profile_v4 details and expected behavior
- Observed tail latency patterns and root cause hypotheses
- Plan for 24h run, telemetry to capture, and acceptance criteria
- Next steps and responsibilities

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: okay everybody thanks for joining, we'll kick off. quick roll call?
[00:12] Evan Park: hey Evan here, ML lead.
[00:15] Carla Mendes: Carla - infra.
[00:18] Sophie Leung: Sophie - product.
[00:21] Alex Morgan: great. Priya and Jordan from our side?
[00:24] Priya Shah: Priya here, i'll be driving the tunings.
[00:26] Jordan Li: Jordan here for any account stuff.
[00:29] Alex Morgan: cool. objective today: review the numbers from the last pilot run, talk through the continuous batching adjustments, and align on the 24h stress run.

[01:05] Priya Shah: quick recap: last week we moved from batch_profile_v2 to v3 which increased max batch window to 24ms and bumped concurrency target to 36, that improved overall throughput by about 12% but we saw P99 spikes around traffic surges. logs suggested some KV cache miss storms.
[01:38] Evan Park: yeah the throughput looked good but during synthetic ramp we saw latency jump from 220ms to 1.2s at the tail which is a problem for the UX team.

[02:10] Carla Mendes: to add, our staging nodes had GC chatter and one of the nodes showed slightly higher PCIe traffic that aligned with the spike times — could be infra-level contention.
[02:34] Priya Shah: interesting, we also noticed queue depth spiking in the request router right before the P99 blip. that suggests batching combining with concurrent token stepping maybe exhausting kernel threads.

[03:00] Sophie Leung: can you explain "concurrent token stepping" — just so product understands the knob?
[03:07] Priya Shah: yeah sorry, bad phrasing. what i mean is concurrency of inference pipelines: we allow N in-flight requests to the model adaptor, each pulls KV cache, runs attention kernels. if concurrency is too high, memory movement and PCIe stalls can compound and misses amplify latency.

[03:45] Alex Morgan: thanks. Priya, you pushed a new variant overnight? what changed in v4?
[03:52] Priya Shah: v4 is conservative: reduces max concurrency target to 28 from 36, shortens batch window to 16ms, and enables a soft-prefetch for KV cache which keeps a small warm set for high-frequency prefixes. also changes backoff in router so queueing builds slower rather than bursting.
[04:20] Evan Park: soft-prefetch sounds promising — were hit rates simulated?
[04:26] Priya Shah: yes, on historical traffic we saw KV hit improve from ~64% to ~82% for the sampled prompt set. synthetic stress still needed.

[05:01] Alex Morgan: ok can you show the dashboard numbers from the v4 test?
[05:06] Priya Shah: i'll share screen — dashboard link in chat. (pause) all right top-line: throughput steady at 1.14x baseline, average latency down slightly, p99 improved from 1.2s to ~420ms in the short 2-hour run, and CPU/PCIe stalls reduced.
[05:48] Evan Park: that p99 is better but still above our internal target of 300ms. that 420ms happened during a sudden QPS spike we injected. any idea why not lower?
[06:07] Priya Shah: two hypotheses: remaining cold prefixes that the prefetch didn't cover, and occasional backend NVMe reads when ephemeral KV spilled to disk under peak.
[06:20] Carla Mendes: wait NVMe reads? staging has ephemeral swap on one node, could be our config. we can disable swap and ensure allocation is consistent.
[06:33] Priya Shah: that would help, yes. also hitting high concurrency i think caused tail amplification even with better hit rates.

[07:10] Alex Morgan: let's annotate that as infra action item — Carla to check swap and PCIe error counters.

[07:22] Carla Mendes: noted, i'll run checks after this call.

[07:30] Sophie Leung: what's the risk to our client-facing SLA if we reduce concurrency to 28? are we dropping throughput?
[07:40] Priya Shah: we saw a small throughput bump with v4 even though concurrency lowered — because efficiency per request improved due to higher cache hits and smaller batch wait. it's a net win for cost per token.
[07:55] Evan Park: cost is important but product wants latency guarantees. if lowering concurrency decreases throughput during sustained high QPS, we might need dedicated burst nodes.
[08:12] Alex Morgan: that's where burst capacity comes in — Alex (that's me) will share pricing and options for reserved burst capacity with predictable P99 ceilings.

[08:30] Evan Park: good. another observation: we saw queueing linger in the router for ~120-150ms before dispatch — can you explain router backoff changes in v4?
[08:45] Priya Shah: yes, previously router allowed queue to grow quickly to fill batch windows; v4 introduces exponential soft-backoff that limits queue growth and triggers earlier dispatch if queue latency threshold exceeded. that avoids multi-stage piling.
[09:12] Priya Shah: the tradeoff is slightly more smaller batches, but fewer long tails.

[09:30] Evan Park: can we tune the threshold? like 80ms or 100ms?
[09:35] Priya Shah: absolutely — we kept it at 120ms for v4 to be conservative. we can run A/B with 80ms and 100ms in the 24h run.

[10:02] Alex Morgan: Jordan, from a timeline perspective, customer wants a go/no-go decision by next Tue — is that right Sophie?
[10:12] Sophie Leung: yes we'd like to freeze infra decisions and pricing by Feb 27.

[10:20] Jordan Li: noted, we'll aim to have perf artifacts and pricing before then.

[11:00] Priya Shah: back to root cause: KV spill to disk — i recommend we (1) eliminate swap on staging nodes (Carla), (2) extend the soft-prefetch to include top-2 prefixes per user, (3) lower concurrency target to 24 in one experiment.
[11:26] Evan Park: lowering to 24 — won't that hurt throughput?
[11:30] Priya Shah: likely small hit in synthetic steady state but will drastically reduce tail during spikes. if the customer workload tolerates slightly lower max throughput but needs tighter P99, that's the knob.

[12:00] Carla Mendes: we'll disable swap and also bump staging NVMe performance profile to high. i'll coordinate with infra ops.

[12:18] Priya Shah: great. i'm updating batch_profile_v4 -> batch_profile_v4a with the 24 concurrency and extended prefetch; i'll push to staging after Carla confirms swap disabled.

[12:35] Evan Park: what telemetry should we capture during the 24h run so we can make a deterministic decision?
[12:40] Priya Shah: capture P50/P95/P99 latencies, per-prefix KV hit rate, queue depth distribution, PCIe stalls metric, and percent of requests that hit the soft-prefetch set. also token-level cost per request.

[13:04] Alex Morgan: and keep logs for 5xxs, any OOMs, and kernel-level IO waits. Jordan will push an enriched dashboard link.

[13:20] Jordan Li: link posted in chat — will add annotations for the run windows.

[14:00] Evan Park: if the 24h run shows P99 under 300ms with concurrency 24 and no extra infra, then product is happy; if not we probably need burst capacity or dedicated nodes.

[14:20] Sophie Leung: yes, product's gating metric is P99 < 300ms for interactive user flows, throughput target is secondary within 10% of today.

[14:40] Priya Shah: understood — we'll run two arms in staging: arm A = v4a (concurrency 24, prefetch extended), arm B = v4b (concurrency 28, prefetch extended, router threshold 80ms). compare tails and per-token cost.

[15:05] Evan Park: timeline for that?
[15:09] Priya Shah: planning to push v4a today after Carla disables swap; run starts tomorrow 00:00 UTC and will run 24 hours. v4b will run in the following 24h window.

[15:30] Carla Mendes: i can disable swap tonight and report back here.

[16:00] Alex Morgan: excellent. any blockers on instrumentation?
[16:05] Priya Shah: we added a plugin to log per-prefix hits, but we need customer to share a representative prompt set so we can map prefixes. Evan, can you share the sample prompt file?
[16:17] Evan Park: yes, i'll upload to the shared drive after the call.

[16:30] Sophie Leung: one more ask: can we get a simple SLO report format to show to execs? something like P99, uptime, and cost delta?
[16:41] Jordan Li: i'll template a one-pager and attach to the follow-up email.

[17:00] Alex Morgan: okay let's recap action items quickly. Priya?
[17:06] Priya Shah: Priya: push v4a, validate, and monitor KV hit rates; Evan to run 24h; Carla to disable swap and prep staging; Alex to send pricing and credits; Jordan to post dashboard and SLO one-pager; all to review results and reconvene end of run.

[17:38] Evan Park: sounds good. one quick question — any concerns about data residency if we enable extended prefetch?
[17:45] Priya Shah: prefetch only stores hashed prefixes in memory, no raw user text persisted. but we can scrub identifiers; i'll document the behavior in the security note.

[18:05] Carla Mendes: i'll also check with security on retention settings.

[18:20] Sophie Leung: ok thanks all. schedule next sync? same time next week?
[18:27] Alex Morgan: yes let's tentatively book same time next Friday — we'll cancel if we have to act faster.

[18:40] Alex Morgan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links and timeline. bye.

End of transcript.

References and links shared in chat: dashboard link (redwood-perf-dashboard://blue-harbor/pilot/2026-02-20), batch_profile_v4a config note (link to docs), shared prompt set (drive://blue-harbor/pilot-samples).
